ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, United Nations Security Council sanctions, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, and Public Safety Canada's consolidated sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates, consistent with FINTRAC guidance under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Screened parties must be continuously monitored through a commercial AML screening platform for the duration of the corporate relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries - Corporate Online (https://www.bcregistry.gov.bc.ca) and the OneStop Business Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; if the desired name is in a non-Latin script, a transliteration into English or French must be submitted. The name must include a corporate legal element, such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or the full equivalent, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporate or registered business name in British Columbia.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the rejection notice, accompanied by written submissions, any consent of the body that governs the prohibited word, and alternative name choices. If the Registrar maintains the rejection, the applicant may apply for judicial review to the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 166.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this low-risk e-commerce business, provided that the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in British Columbia, agrees to receive service of process as the registered office, and is authorized to act as a registered office under the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - quantified risk below 5% in the first year of operation. BC Registries does not conduct routine physical inspections for online retail registrants. Canada Revenue Agency may conduct tax audits but unannounced physical inspections are rare for a business with no physical premise of operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 10 (delivery of notice of articles and articles), 11 (incorporation agreement), 17 (correction of articles) and 27 (alteration of articles); Business Corporations Regulation, BC Reg 418/2003 for prescribed forms
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 Incorporation Agreement and Form 2 Notice of Articles, delivered electronically through BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Business Corporations Act; the authorized capital may consist of one or more classes of shares without par value as stated in the Notice of Articles, and no escrow or statutory deposit account is mandated. Issued shares need not be fully paid at incorporation unless the Incorporation Agreement provides otherwise.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscription by the sole founding subscriber for one (1) common share without par value, for the consideration stated in the Incorporation Agreement, is accepted; the share shall be entered in the share register and the share certificate issued; (2) the registered office of the company is established at the address stated in the Notice of Articles, and the records office is maintained at the registered records keeper's address; (3) the following officers are appointed, serving at the pleasure of the board: President, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer; (4) the directors and officers are authorized to open banking accounts, retain the corporate service provider, and execute the necessary documents. DATED this ___ day of ____________, 20___.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation through the NUANS System
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online / OneStop Business Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name to a BC Registry-authorized NUANS search provider or enter it directly on Corporate Online. If clear, reserve the name for 56 days by filing the name reservation application and paying the fee; the resulting Name Reservation Response is required for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with a distinctive element and legal element (Inc. or Corp.)
NUANS name search report issued within 56 days
Name reservation application and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusing or contrary to regulations, file alternative names on a fresh NUANS report, request reconsideration by the Assistant Registrar of Companies, or proceed with incorporation number and apply later for a name change under s. 27 of the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation by Filing the Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, BC Registries and Online Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation application through BC Corporate Online, specifying the authorized share structure, registered office address, and first directors. Attach the Form 1 Incorporation Agreement and Form 2 Notice of Articles, pay the CAD 350 fee, and transmit the filing. The Registrar will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and assign a BC company number upon acceptance.
required_dossiers: Form 2 Notice of Articles setting out the authorized share structure, registered office and first directors
Name reservation response or consent to an incorporation number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the deficiencies through Corporate Online within 14 days; post-issuance defects are cured by delivering a corrected Notice of Articles and articles under s. 17, or by filing an alteration under s. 27, of the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and GST/HST Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Business Registration Online (OneStop / CRA Business Window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated company for its 9-digit Business Number and elect to open a GST/HST program account where the online retail activity exceeds the $30,000 small supplier threshold or where voluntary registration is desired. Submit the application using the BC company number and corporate particulars.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation or State of Information (Registry Extract)
Corporate name, registered office, and directors' particulars
Business activity description and expected gross revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN or program account application is incomplete, call the CRA Business Window to amend the account; the delay does not affect statutory corporate existence and registration can be backdated to the incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Adoption: First Board Resolution, Share Certificates and Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The first directors named in the Notice of Articles convene a directors' meeting and adopt the organizational resolution confirming share subscription and issuance, adoption of the registered office address, appointment of officers, approval of banking mandates, and authorization of the corporate service provider. All minutes are entered in the corporate minute book kept at the BC records office.
required_dossiers: Minute book and corporate records binder
Blank share certificates or scrip certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: This is an internal corporate act; any omission is ratified by a subsequent directors' or shareholders' resolution and no action with the Registrar is required unless the Notice of Articles itself must be corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Ongoing Annual Return Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver Business Licence Office (or competent BC municipality) and BC Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the municipal business licence applicable to online retail warehousing and distribution of hydroponics and gardening equipment, confirming zoning, storage and display conditions. Maintain annual filing obligations under the Business Corporations Act by submitting the Form 3 Annual Report within two months after each anniversary of incorporation to avoid involuntary dissolution.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and State of Information
Description of goods sold and premises use
Municipal business licence application and fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is refused, appeal through the municipality's licensing appeal mechanism or adjust the premises description; corporate non-compliance is cured by filing the overdue annual report with the prescribed late fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Technical Safety BC (formerly BC Safety Authority) and WorkSafeBC for premises-related clearances; no sectoral manufacturing board applies to pure e-commerce retailing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - the undertaking is online retail and distribution, not manufacturing; a municipal business licence and, where applicable, a Technical Safety BC electrical permit for warehouse/showroom fit-out are the only operating authorizations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada / Impact Assessment Agency of Canada and BC Ministry of Environment and Parks
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no full EIA report or registration mandated under the Impact Assessment Act, SC 2019, c. 28 or the BC Environmental Assessment Act; retail warehousing and distribution of hydroponics equipment is not a designated activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC process emissions arise; compliance is limited to municipal stormwater and sewer bylaws for the warehouse, the BC Recycling Regulation (BC Reg 449/2004) for e-waste, batteries and packaging, and the BC Clean Coast Clean Waters Act for plastic packaging waste handling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and inspection under the BC Fire Code, including sprinkler protection and storage-height limits for the retail warehouse; structural load inspection for high-density racking; and WorkSafeBC occupational health-and-safety clearance together with electrical safety verification under the Safety Standards Act, SBC 2003, c. 39.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal fiscal authority for GST/HST, payroll, and federal corporate income tax (portal: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency; My Business Account at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html). The Province of British Columbia administers the separate Provincial Sales Tax (PST) and BC corporate income tax via the Ministry of Finance (Consumer Taxation Branch; portal: eTaxBC at etax.gov.bc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A domestically incorporated CBCA/BCBCA corporation is auto-issued a nine-digit Business Number (BN) with an 'RC' corporate income tax program account upon incorporation, transmitted by Corporations Canada or the BC Registry to the CRA. The entity must then register for the GST/HST 'RT' program account through Business Registration Online (BRO) or My Business Account; registration is compulsory once taxable supplies made in Canada exceed C$30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the aggregate of the four preceding consecutive quarters (Excise Tax Act s. 148 small supplier rule), and is otherwise available voluntarily. A foreign non-resident entity soliciting orders or carrying on business in Canada obtains a BN by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) through BRO and registers for GST/HST in the same manner, or, if selling tangible goods through a Canadian fulfillment warehouse, under the 2021 GST/HST e-commerce vendor registration rules. For BC PST, the seller must register with the BC Ministry of Finance through eTaxBC using the same BN; registration is mandatory once taxable sales in BC exceed C$10,000 in the preceding 12 months (Provincial Sales Tax Act small seller exemption), with marketplace facilitators deemed to be the PST-collecting seller for marketplace orders from May 1, 2023. Payment processors such as Stripe and PayPal are not 'marketplace facilitators' and do not relieve the seller of registration obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Business Corporation is a corporation resident in Canada under the Income Tax Act, subject to tax on worldwide income at the federal (15% general / 9% small business) and BC provincial (12% general / 2% small business) rates; no pass-through eligibility. If Canadian-controlled and private (CCPC), the first C$500,000 of active business income qualifies for the federal/BC small business deduction, subject to the aggregate business limit and specified corporate group rules. The tax base is residency-based worldwide taxation; there is no Canadian territorial remittance election for corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no check-the-box or entity-classification election in Canadian tax law; foreign entity tax classifications (e.g., US disregarded-entity elections) have no CRA effect. Available elections include: (1) voluntary GST/HST registration by a non-resident not carrying on business in Canada (Excise Tax Act s. 240(2.1)); (2) the Excise Tax Act s. 156 'nil consideration' election between closely related corporations (Form GST25-1); (3) the GST Quick Method election (Form GST74) and annual filing elections; (4) the Income Tax Act s. 216 election for a non-resident's Canadian rental or timber income; and (5) for BC PST, the small-seller voluntary registration and vendor allowance election. Canada's hybrid mismatch rules (Income Tax Act ss. 18.4–18.6, enacted 2024) impose a mechanical deduction-denial framework without taxpayer elections, and relevant hybrid instruments are recharacterized by statute.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual VAT/retail sales tax system: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST — a value-added tax under Excise Tax Act Part IX) at 5%, coupled with the British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST — a retail sales and use tax) at 7%; effective combined rate of 12% on most taxable tangible personal property sold at retail in BC. BC is not an HST province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: C$30,000 CAD — triggered when a registrant's taxable supplies made in Canada exceed C$30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in the aggregate of the last four consecutive calendar quarters (small supplier threshold). BC PST: C$10,000 CAD — a 'small seller' whose taxable sales in BC in the preceding 12 months do not exceed C$10,000 is exempt from PST registration; registration becomes mandatory above this threshold, and the threshold applies to the seller's own sales before any deemed marketplace-facilitator shift.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoice stamping, or tax-authority API validation regime at either the federal or BC level; indirect tax compliance is self-assessed on periodic GST/HST/PST returns. Mandatory electronic filing applies to GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding C$1.5M (GST NETFILE) and to corporations with gross revenue exceeding C$1M for T2 returns. The voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (Peppol PINT standard) is optional and does not displace the Excise Tax Act invoice-content and records-retention duties (ETA ss. 236 and 286).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% GST/HST applies to exported goods under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, Part V (section 1) where a GST/HST registrant supplies goods to a non-resident purchaser, ships or delivers the goods to a common carrier, postal service, or courier destined to a point outside Canada, the goods are exported as soon as the circumstances permit, and the registrant retains contemporaneous export evidence. Services (e.g., software configurations) are zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident not registered under the ETA and the benefit of the service is received outside Canada (Schedule VI, Part V, section 7). Hydroponics and gardening equipment (HS 9406, 8419, 8421) are not export-controlled, but an Export Control List / General Export Permit screening should be documented. BC PST does not apply to goods validly exported, and PST-registered vendors may claim refunds of PST paid on goods subsequently exported within the prescribed periods under the BC Provincial Sales Tax Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export report under the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES/Y50), mandatory for exports valued over C$2,000 or controlled goods; for US-bound parcel traffic, courier ACI export data or AES proof in lieu
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or courier manifest showing delivery to an outside-Canada destination
Commercial invoice and itemized packing list
Purchase order or sales contract with the non-resident buyer
Inward remittance evidence — bank SWIFT advice, foreign-invoice remittance certificate, or Stripe/PayPal settlement statement in CAD-equivalent reflecting receipt of export proceeds
GST/HST return and working papers supporting the 0% rate and input tax credit claims
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; for this dossier the 180-day benchmark is adopted as the internal export-evidence control, requiring export proceeds to be reconciled and documented within 180 days of shipment. In audits, CRA scrutinizes zero-rating substantiation in GST/HST net-file reviews and post-assessment verification programs. Failure of documentation reverses the 0% rate, yielding assessments of 5% unremitted GST plus daily compound arrears interest, with BC PST assessments for supplies not validly exported, and: (1) a 50% false-statement penalty under ETA s. 285(1) for knowing or grossly negligent misstatements; (2) a 50% evasion penalty under ETA s. 280(1) (minimum C$100); (3) an unlimited look-back period under ETA s. 298(4) overriding the normal four-year limitation where misrepresentation or fraud exists; (4) criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327 or Criminal Code s. 380 with fines up to twice the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment; and (5) BC PST civil penalties up to 25% of tax evaded, plus interest and potential registration cancellation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) together with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); currency issuance and monetary policy reside with BoC, while financial institution supervision falls under OSFI.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible current and capital account regime with no material exchange controls. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is freely permitted under the Canada Business Corporations Act and Income Tax Act, subject only to corporate tax clearance (CG-28 or equivalent non-resident withholding tax compliance) and anti-money-laundering documentation. Dividend repatriation may be affected by Part XIII withholding tax unless reduced by treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirements exist in Canada. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted freely; no mandatory conversion ratio or holding-period constraint applies. Reporting to the Canada Revenue Agency is limited to income tax and GST/HST obligations, and no foreign-exchange repatriation declaration is required under federal law.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Short-Term Liquidity Facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for low-risk e-commerce treasury operations, subject to full money services business (MSB) registration with FINTRAC and provincial registration where required (e.g., British Columbia's Money Services Act if regulated). Non-resident EMIs must establish a Canadian legal entity, appoint a compliance officer, implement a FINTRAC-approved AML/ATF program, and maintain a clearing relationship with a Canadian bank. Remote-only EMIs may be used for pay-in/pay-out, but must not hold client funds in Canada without appropriate licensing; a regulated Schedule I bank account remains the primary treasury anchor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a British Columbia business corporation, the majority of Canadian Schedule I banks permit full remote onboarding for low-risk e-commerce entities using verifiable digital identification and video-conference interviews. Directors and ultimate beneficial owners may complete the interview remotely if identity document verification, utility bills or proof of address, and corporate registry extracts are submitted. However, some account types, particularly those requiring a corporate credit facility, may require a physical branch visit or an in-person signature, but standard operational accounts can be opened without physical presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk source-of-wealth or source-of-funds for initial capital injection from a foreign jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate certificate of good standing from the foreign registry; audited or management-prepared financial statements; bank reference letter from the remitting institution; notarized board resolution confirming the source of funds; gift or shareholder loan agreement; evidence of tax compliance in the remitting country; and a sworn beneficial ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent or incomplete Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) identification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed FINTRAC UBO form; corporate register extract showing all shareholders; organisational chart tracing direct and indirect ownership; passport copies of each 25%-or-more shareholder; proof of residential address for directors and UBOs; and utility bills or bank statements not older than 90 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce payment flow ambiguity (mixed Stripe/PayPal settlement and cross-border intercompany transfers)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction flow diagram; executed e-commerce marketplace agreements; payment processor (Stripe/PayPal) settlement statements; inventory purchase invoices and logistics documentation; and a written compliance manual explaining that payment processors act as payment facilitators rather than deposit-taking institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media screening matches on directors or corporate counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Professional name-screening report from a reputable provider; nationality and residency documentary proof; written explanation of any homonym matches; legal opinion from Canadian counsel clarifying no prohibited dealings; and evidence that no transacting party is listed on the OSFI/AMF sanctions list or UN sanctions list.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound equity injection is executed via SWIFT MT103 wire from the foreign shareholder's bank to the Canadian corporation's operational account at a Schedule I bank. The wire message must clearly indicate the corporate legal name, Canadian account number, bank institution number and transit number, and a reference to the share subscription or shareholder loan agreement. There is no mandatory Canadian purpose code, but the bank may request a letter of explanation and a board resolution to satisfy internal AML/CFT controls. For incoming payments exceeding CAD 10,000, the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) and Common Reporting Standard (CRS) self-certification must be on file. The bank will verify the entity's registration with Corporations Canada or the British Columbia Registrar of Companies, and may ask for supporting audited financials for capital validation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for garden hydroponics equipment are cleared primarily via bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 transfers for low-value spot payments and Documentary Letters of Credit (LC) for high-value inventory procurement. LCs are issued under UCP600 rules through Canadian confirming banks for suppliers in Asia or North America. The treasury operation should maintain a CAD-denominated operational account for local disbursements, a USD-denominated account for cross-border supplier settlements, and make use of payment rails such as Visa Direct, Fedwire, and EFT for non-SWIFT mass payouts. All outbound wire instructions require AML triggers such as recipient name, address, account, and, where applicable, the supplier's business identification number. The company is subject to the Income Tax Act and GST/HST reporting on importations, and must retain customs entry documentation for potential CRA audits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla foreign currency forwards (CAD/USD and CAD/CNY) entered into with Canadian Schedule I banks under ISDA Master Agreements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies where local deliverability is restricted or illiquid, subject to bank counterparty policy and internal hedging mandate
Currency swaps (cross-currency interest rate swaps) for medium-term balance-sheet hedging of intercompany debt or acquisition financing
FX options (to be used limited to costless collar or put-spread structures) for protection against CAD volatility on committed trade payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (Corporate Registry Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Registries, Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within two months after each anniversary date of incorporation; filing during the anniversary month qualifies for the reduced fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Base late fee CAD 57, escalating on a statutory scale with each additional two-month delay; failure to file for two consecutive years renders the company liable to administrative strike-off by the Registrar after notice; certificates of good standing are withheld while a return is overdue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (includes BC provincial corporate income tax, Schedule 50 Shareholder Information, and CCPC schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due six months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end files by June 30); tax balance-due day is two months after year-end, extended to three months for a CCPC eligible for the small business deduction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of delay (maximum 12 months) with a minimum CAD 100 penalty; daily arrears interest compounded; repeated failure may trigger CRA enforcement action and criminal prosecution for wilful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (Form 4006) under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation, but applicable only if the entity is incorporated federally under the CBCA rather than as a BC provincial company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years allows Corporations Canada to dissolve the corporation by administrative process; reinstatement requires a resolution, creditor notice, and added filing fees.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under the BC Business Corporations Act for a private corporation; an audit is triggered only by the articles, a unanimous shareholder agreement, a lending covenant, or a securities distribution. There is no revenue-or-asset-based audit threshold for a private e-commerce retailer.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook – Accounting Part II); ASPE is the customary standard for private enterprises, with IFRS permitted; either framework is accepted by the CRA for T2 reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC has no public UBO annual filing; the BC Annual Report confirms directors only. Share transfers are recorded continuously in the securities register. From May 1, 2025, BC companies must maintain an internal Transparency Register of individuals with significant control (25% or more of voting rights or shares), refreshed by reasonable steps at least once every 12 months and produced to the Registrar, police, or CRA on demand. A federally incorporated CBCA entity must instead maintain and annually confirm an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register every 12 months.
